title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
The page defines an 'oriented' variant of a combinatorial structure M. The machine transcription reads the title as 'Magnets'; the handwriting may instead be 'Maquettes', so the reading is uncertain. The structure carries relations between its elements: a 'circled' order ≤°, a relation ≪° and an incidence/opposition relation |°|. Judging from context, these are combinatorial models of (tame) stratified or cellular spaces, with elements graded by dimension.

Definition: M is oriented when x ≪° y implies x = y, and x |°| y implies x ≠ y.

Example in dimension ≤ 1. Here ≪° is the identity, so the first condition is automatic, and the second requires x |°| y ⇒ x ≠ y. Write S = M_0^+ ('sommets', vertices) and A = M_1 ('arêtes orientées', oriented edges). The relation |°| on A gives a fixed-point-free involution σ: A → A, reversal of orientation. The relation ≤° gives a map A → S, the origin of an oriented edge. Conclusion: oriented structures of dimension ≤ 1 are the same as graphs, in exactly Serre's sense from 'Arbres, amalgames': (S, A, a fixed-point-free involution on A, and an origin map A → S).

A largely illegible NB remarks that this structure (orientation) is not defined anew for a general M but is induced from the dimension-≤1 pieces, or from 'quantities' attached to them.

The page then sets a programme: in the oriented case of dimension 2, one should recover the description of 2-dimensional combinatorial objects, probably the combinatorial maps ('cartes') of the Esquisse d'un programme, i.e. permutation/flag-type descriptions. The overall aim is to show that the general axiomatics of these structures specialises to the classical combinatorial encodings of graphs (dim 1) and maps on surfaces (dim 2).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The identification with graphs is plausible given σ fixed-point-free and the origin map, but the page does not check that the remaining axioms of M impose no further constraints (e.g. loops, multiple edges), which Serre's definition allows.
The dimension-2 case is only announced, not carried out.

ideas.what: Oriented structures of dim ≤1 are equivalent to graphs given as vertices, oriented edges, a fixed-point-free involution and an origin map
ideas.where_published: Serre, Arbres, amalgames, SL2 (Astérisque 46, 1977); Grothendieck uses similar graph encodings in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Axiomatic combinatorial models (relations ≤°, ≪°, |°|) of stratified/cellular spaces, with a notion of orientation defined by the conditions x≪°y⇒x=y and x|°|y⇒x≠y
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial models of tame spaces; close to abstract polytopes, regular CW posets, face posets with flag structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Various (Björner for CW posets; McMullen–Schulte for abstract polytopes)
ideas.where_published: Only in unpublished Analysis situs notes (cote 156), as far as known

ideas.what: Programme: the oriented dimension-2 case should recover the combinatorial description of maps on surfaces
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial maps / cartographic groups (permutation triples, hypermaps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Edmonds, Tutte, Jacques, Cori; Grothendieck's Esquisse d'un programme; Jones–Singerman (1978)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), sections on 'cartes' and the cartographic group

missed.claim: Grothendieck intended a single axiomatics of combinatorial 'magnets/maquettes' that specialises in dim 1 to Serre graphs and in dim 2 to combinatorial maps. The dim-2 verification is announced but not done on this page.
missed.quote: Cas de dim 2 [...] orientés, on [...] trouver la description [...] combinatoires de dim ≤ 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links the 1986 tame-topology programme to the dessins/maps formalism of the Esquisse. A uniform poset-with-relations axiomatics of oriented cell structures, specialising to maps, would interest people working on combinatorial maps in higher dimension (n-maps, Lienhardt's generalized maps). Whether the neighbouring pages complete this is unknown.

deep.surprise_reason: The concrete content is Serre's definition of a graph, recovered as a special case. The only mildly interesting point is the unpublished framework and the intended link to combinatorial maps, which matches known Esquisse themes.
transcription_corrections: The title word read as 'Magnets' may be 'Maquettes' ('Maquettes orientées'); the handwriting is ambiguous.
Line 2 likely reads 'Ex: Les systèmes de M en dim ≤ 1' (or similar) rather than 'Les {magnets} de dim ≤1'.
The struck-out 'M = M_0^+' and 'On pose' are consistent with the image; the parenthetical notes are '(sommets)' and '(arêtes orientées)'.
The bracket after A →° S reads approximately '[donnée par la relation ≤°]'; a marginal note adds '(≤ 1 ?)' near it.
The NB lines are largely illegible; 'défini de nouveau' and 'par des quantités' are guesses.
